A salt flat under noon sun, white crust cracked into polygons to every horizon, blinding reflected light from below, a single thunderhead distant and dark, the air perfectly still.
A deep jungle river at night, black water reflecting tangled moonlit canopy, fireflies threading through the roots, the river bending into impenetrable green shadow where the current disappears.
A coastal sea-cave at high tide, dark water surging across ribbed stone, shafts of turquoise light angling through a flooded entrance, foam hissing in crevices, the tide pulling back.
A high alpine meadow at the snowline, wildflowers crowding the last soil before ice, a cold blue sky pressing down, granite peaks raking cloud above, silence broken only by wind.
A smouldering ashfield after wildfire, blackened trunks standing in pale grey ash, a sullen orange glow still throbbing at the tree-line, smoke drifting low across scorched and smoking ground.
A fog-drowned estuary at dawn, mudflats gleaming, reed-beds fading into grey nothing, a diffuse sun barely brightening the milk-white horizon, still water holding a ghost of its own reflection.
A celestial void of drifting nebula, deep violet and cold blue gas swirling around distant star-cores, dust-lanes cutting darkness, the whole field glowing with ancient scattered stellar light.
